description.narrative:
Insatsen avser ett kärnstöd till organisationen WITNESS.
WITNESS arbetar globalt för att stödja marginaliserade och utsatta grupper att använda video och informations- och kommunikationsteknologi (IKT) för att stärka deras möjligheter att delta i samhället, stärka rättssäkerheten och skydda och försvara mänskliga rättigheter.
Insatsen övergripande mål är att tillse att de miljoner utsatta och marginaliserade grupper som använder video och IKT för att åstadkomma förändring kan göra detta på ett säkert, etiskt och effektivt sätt. Detta mål ska åstadkommas genom följande planerade resultat: 1) Fattiga och marginaliserade grupper, människorättsförsvarare, media aktivister, journalister och jurister har stärkt förmåga och kapacitet att använda video och IKT på ett säkert, etiskt och effektivt sätt för att stärka mänskliga rättigheter 2) Ekosystemet för mänskliga rättigheter på lokal, regional och global nivå samt mellan gräsrötter och relevanta aktörer på systemnivå har stärkts 3) Personer som använder teknologiska system och IKT för MR-aktivism kan göra detta på ett säkert och effektivt sätt. 4) WITNESS institutionella kapacitet, mångfald och resiliens för att kunna agera som sammankallare, facilitator, försvarare och kunskapsnav har stärkts, för att kunna stödja deras strategiska vision och programmål. De fyra största givarna till WITNESS är Sida, Ford Foundation, Oak Foundation and MacArthur Foundation.

The contribution concerns a core support to the organisation WITNESS.
The overall objective of the contribution is to empower marginalized and vulnerable communities worldwide using video and information and communications technology (ICT) to realize opportunities to participate in society, improve access to justice and protect and defend human rights. This overall objective should be realized through the following expected outcomes:
-Poor and marginalized communities, human rights defenders, media activists, journalists and lawyers have increased skills and capacity to use video and ICTs safely, ethically, and effectively for human rights change -The broader human rights ecosystem is strengthened between the local, regional and international levels, as well as between grassroots and systems-level stakeholders -At risk-users can more safely and effectively use technology systems and ICTs for human rights activism -WITNESS institutional capacity, diversity and resilience to act as a convener, facilitator, supporter and knowledge hub is strengthened, in order to support its strategic vision and programmatic goals The four largest donors to WITNESS are Sida, Ford Foundation, Oak Foundation and MacArthur Foundation.

The overarching objective of the intervention is to ensure that the millions of vulnerable and marginalized communities turning to video and ICTs to create change worldwide can do so safely, ethically, and effectively. To contribute to the overarching objective the following four expected outcomes of the intervention have been identified:1) Poor and marginalized communities, human rights defenders, media activists, journalists and lawyers have increased skills and capacity to use video and ICTs safely, ethically, and effectively for human rights change 2) The broader human rights ecosystem is strengthened between the local, regional and international levels, as well as between grassroots and systems-level stakeholders 3) At risk-users can more safely and effectively use technology systems and ICTs for human rights activism4) WITNESS’ institutional capacity, diversity and resilience to act as a convener, facilitator, supporter and knowledge hub is strengthened, in order to support its strategic vision and programmatic goals

description.narrative: WITNESS continues to plays a capacity building and support role to grassroots partners seeking to incorporate video and ICTs in their efforts to combat a range of human rights violations. During the reporting period Witness are reporting the following results: Witness resources and guidance has generated 2,979,785 online engagements and 65,458 resource downloads Witness has 22 new or adapted resources on topics such as state violence, environmental violations, internet shutdowns, election violence, and gender based violence Conducted 35 trainings (inperson & virtual) with 871 grassroots actors trained to augment skills and knowledge around the use of video and ICTs to protect democracy and human rights Organised 80 convenings, workshops/feedback sessions, or coalition/ campaign efforts to ensure participation of grassroots groups and ensure prioritization of their needs 5 research analyses articulating the benefits and harms of technologies on marginalized communities and proposed solutions 9 surge responses, including a sustained response to the invasion of Ukraine 57 advocacy meetings with C2PA, Microsoft, Google, Google Search, YouTube, Twitter, Adobe, Meta/Facebook, and TikTok To illustrate the change Witness has also reported the following examples: Sustained surge response following Russias unlawful invasion of Ukraine: In a conflict marked by widespread human rights violations and war crimes, and rife with disinformation and manipulated media, the importance of capturing and preserving trusted, authentic accounts cannot be underestimated. We continued to train journalists, lawyers, and volunteer documenters of war crimes to ensure that the documentation, curation, and presentation of evidence is impactful and verifiable. We also expanded our relationship with a key partner organization, Ukrainian Legal Advisory Group (ULAG), collaborating with them on a train the trainers (ToT) strategy that was received with widespread gratitude from participants and supporting ULAGs participation in the Assembly of State Parties (ASP) to advocate for support to Ukrainian civil society. Right to Record global campaign: In November of 2022, WITNESS launched its Right to Record global campaign: Right to Record: Protest. Resist. Exist. The right to record, which is recognized by the United Nations, is the right to film state actors like police, military, or other law enforcement officials without fear of arrest, violence or forms of retaliation. The wideranging campaign included a blog post to accompany the launch, an explainer video featuring our staff, and the sharing of resources created in partnership with the Brazilian independent newsroom Canal Reload. Witness also copublished a report in collaboration with partner Documenta to shed light on protective frameworks when exercising the right to record. Strategic Communications for Land Defense: Recognizing the power of collaboration to bolster impact, Witness explored opportunities for lessons, experiences, and resources from grassroots land defenders to be shared across regions. From hosting a crossregional Convening on Land Defense Communications Across the Americas (CORAL) in Mexico, to producing a video to expand the emotional impact and overall reach of the Report on the Impact of Non-implementation of the African Commission's Endorois Decision, Witness supported land defense efforts directly in addition to enabling crosspollination among local partners on tactics to defend their land and challenge environmental degradation. Witness also published a Video as Evidence Environmental Defense Guide (Annex 1) to assist communities across the world that are affected by extractive industries to collect highquality, actionable documentation of violations committed by perpetrators. Rohingya Genocide Archive (RGA): WITNESS co-hosted a launch event for the RGA, a Rohingyaled initiative to systematically collect and preserve audiovisual documentation of atrocities against the Rohingya people. The event included the presentation of the RGA, which is only accessible to critical stakeholders, and a new public website that shares the project's methodology and an analysis of how the RGA fits into the more significant movement of community-based human rights archives worldwide. Authenticity Infrastructure & Deepfake Detection: As an organization, Witness continues to pull focus on the harms, threats and opportunities surrounding the development of AI technologies and to hone in on evolving grassroots community needs for access to deepfake detection tools. During the reporting period, Witness launched a pilot initiative called the Deepfake Detection Rapid Response Force, in which WIitness serves as an intermediary to connect local communities who have pieces of media requiring authenticity analysis/verification to deepfake and media forensic experts who can provide the necessary analysis. Witness then work to ensure that insights from the Force directly inform research decisions and policymaking on deepfake detection and access to detection tools at both the platform and governmental levels. In addition to its work on the Rapid Response Force, Witness held a convening to address satire and freedom of expression in the age of deepfakes cohosted a workshop with the Google News Initiative on dealing with deceptive deepfakes in journalism as well as ethical uses of synthetic media in journalism continued to lead the Harms and Threats task force of the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (C2PA) while participating in the Technical Working Group and various additional task forces of the C2PA and collaborated as a lead partner and the sole civil society organization with Partnership on AI (PAI) and other groups to draft the Responsible Practices for Synthetic Media, a framework on how to responsibly develop, create, and share synthetic media that launched in February of 2023.
